title: The Observer Effect in Quantum Mechanics
text:
The observer effect describes the phenomenon where the act of measuring a quantum system inherently influences its state. Before measurement, particles exist in a superposition—a combination of all possible states simultaneously. The process of observation forces the wave function to collapse into a single, definite eigenstate.

This principle challenges classical intuitions regarding objectivity, suggesting that reality at the micro-level is fundamentally probabilistic rather than fixed. It forms a cornerstone concept for understanding quantum measurements and decoherence.
